courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: College of Media Orientation
courses.description: College of Media Orientation is designed to build academic and social integrity and to give students the resources they need to be responsible members of the University of Illinois community who earn degrees in a timely manner.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Sports Media for Majors
courses.description: The course is designed to introduce students to the interdisciplinary nature of the degree, to lay a common foundation for future coursework, to highlight experiential learning opportunities with campus partners, and to explore potential career options. Students will read and analyze reports about the sports media field and participate in group and individual activities.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Subject offerings of new and developing areas of knowledge and practice in the fields of media. The course is intended to augment the existing curriculum. See Class Schedule or college course information for topics and prerequisites. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in the same term to a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary; may be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.
courses.prereqNote: See Class Schedule or college course information for topics and prerequisites.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Watching the Environment
courses.description: This course examines how films portray the health environment and the need for environmental protection. The course focuses on series of questions including: To what extent does a film suggest that the world has environmental concerns? What are the constraints that narrative form, production routines, financing and distribution put on representing environmental problems and environmentalists? Is the information in the film to be trusted? In documentaries, are physical and social scientists’ explanations of environmental problems and solutions reliable? What cues can we use from within and outside the film to evaluate the film for credibility? During the course participants will compare the science and economics of selected environmental issues with film presentations, examine what drives of environmental participation (and the limits of film in presenting science), and look at the constraints of producing special interest versus broad distribution films on presentations of the environment. Class includes viewing blockbuster, Oscar, and award-winning documentaries. Lecture attendance is mandatory. Same as NRES 223.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Undergraduate Open Seminar
courses.description: Experimental course on special topics pertinent to the disciplines studied within the College of Media. Topics will vary. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in the same or separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Media Study Abroad
courses.description: Provides credit toward the undergraduate degree for study at accredited foreign institutions or approved overseas programs. Final determination of credit is made upon the student's completion of the work. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.
courses.prereqText: One year of residence at UIUC; good academic standing, and prior approval of the College of Media.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Special Topics in Media
courses.description: Special topics course focusing on cultural, economic, historical, political, and social themes and issues that influence or are influenced by the media. Topics will vary. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated for a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: One year of Media courses, Junior or senior standing in the College of Media, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Varying topics including the cultural, social, historical, legal, economic, political, and other issues that influence or are influenced by Media. 1 to 3 undergraduate hours. 1 to 3 graduate hours. May be repeated in the same or separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: Previous classes in either AGCM, ADV, JOUR, or MACS.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Media Capstone
courses.description: Students will reflect on what they have learned over the course of their degree program and apply this knowledge and skillset to discussion of current events within the media industry. Students will read and analyze reports about the media field and participate in group and individual activities about careers in media including the development of a plan for their careers in their chosen field. 1 undergraduate hour. No graduate credit.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to students pursuing the online degree of Bachelor of Arts in Media.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Dev Psycholinguistics
courses.description: Examination of empirical and theoretical literature on the acquisition of language; emphasis on universal patterns in the acquisition of a first language and on a consideration of explanations, both psychological and linguistic, for these patterns.
courses.prereqText: LING 425, PSYC 425 or PSYC 462, or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as LING 524 and PSYC 524. See PSYC 524.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Psycholinguistics
courses.description: Critical survey of psychological research on language and communication; emphasis on psychological processes that allow humans to produce and understand speech, writing, and gesture.
courses.pointerText: Same as LING 525 and PSYC 525. See PSYC 525.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Human Experience in Immersive Media: XR, AI, and the Human Condition
courses.description: This graduate level course offers a comprehensive exploration of human experience in immersive media, encompassing not only direct users but also non-users and social others who interact with or are affected by XR and AI environments. Drawing on communication, psychology, design, and ethics, the course maps immersive experience across perceptual, psychological, contextual, social, and cultural dimensions of human experience. Students will engage with theory, empirical research, and practical case studies to understand how immersive systems shape perception, cognition, emotion, relationships, and meaning making in digital society.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Feminist Media Studies
courses.description: Addresses major areas of theoretical debate or interest in the broad topic of "Feminist Media Studies" and looks in depth at a number of theoretical issues which define it. Develops an understanding of historical, psychoanalytic, interpretive, and social scientific approaches to the study of film and television texts, their reception, and their production. Readings are extensive and directed toward illustrating the range of theoretical and empirical approaches applied to addressing questions of central interest in the field. Viewings will emphasize some lesser-known historical texts central to theoretical debates in the field. Viewings and readings are focused on "popular" film and television. Same as GWS 560.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Political Economy of Comm
courses.description: Analyzes the structure, policy, and behavior of such media of communication as newspapers, magazines, books, postal service, telegraph, telephone, broadcasting, and film; special emphasis on their relationships to the political order and the economy.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Popular Culture
courses.description: Examines problems of cultural analysis related to the media of communications and the social implications of communications research.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Proseminar I
courses.description: Addresses the mass media of communications, their role as social institutions, and their control and support. Examines evolution of research on mass media content, audience, and effects.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Proseminar II
courses.description: Addresses the problems of communications, including the individual as a communicating system, symbolic processes, analysis of messages, psycholinguistics, and language as social behavior.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Freedom of Expression
courses.description: Examines the development of the Anglo-American press system and the idea of freedom of the press; explores contemporary mass media and their implications for freedom and democracy.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Cultural Studies and Critical Interpretation
courses.description: Explores the history, applications and limitations of various theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of contemporary culture and popular media. Examines debates and issues within cultural studies and with other schools of thought. The impact of cultural studies across the disciplines.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Philosophy of Technology
courses.description: Introduces students to those thinkers who understand technology philosophically as a central component in modern culture. Examines major perspectives on the nature of technology, rooted in Norbert Weiner, Karl Marx, and Martin Heidegger. Links media technologies, information systems, and global communications background problems and basic issues to technology more generally. Develops instrumentalism, feminist and critical approaches, ethical concerns, and alternative technologies in the context of technology as a cultural activity.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Communication Ethics
courses.description: This course introduces the latest literature in, or directly relevant to, communication, media and information ethics. It examines current efforts in applied and professional ethics, feminist ethics, and social ethics to develop ethical models that are cross-cultural, gender inclusive and international. The major ethical issues are considered in such areas as global communication, new media technologies, information systems, news, and entertainment.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: May be repeated in the same or in multiple semesters if topics vary.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Quantitative Methods
courses.description: Introduces the methods of empirical research in the behavioral sciences applicable to research problems in human communication, with emphasis on studies of mass communication. Lectures, readings, and laboratory practice.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Qualitative Methods
courses.description: Introduces qualitative concepts and strategies in the social sciences and humanities which apply to research problems in mass communications.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: ICR Colloquium
courses.description: Weekly presentations and discussion centered around Institute of Communications Research faculty research and graduate student professionalization in the field of Communications and Media. May be repeated in separate terms.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to students with Graduate class standing.

courses.subject: MDIA
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in the same term or in separate terms up to a maximum of 16 hours.
